stem: Ritu says a whole number is divisible by $10$ exactly when its units digit is $0$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly explains why this last-digit shortcut works?

options.text: Units digit is the name of the rule, so that label is the reason.
Every higher place value in a whole number is a multiple of $10$, so only the units digit can affect divisibility by $10$.
The units digit produces place value, so place value comes from the units digit alone.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Expanding by place value, tens and above are multiples of 10, so divisibility by 10 depends only on the units digit.

teacher.key_rationale: Higher places are multiples of 10, so only the units digit matters. Naming "units digit" swaps the reason for a label. Saying the units digit produces place value reverses the expansion.
